📘 Planar Unit-Distance Discovery Docs

A CMCC semantic mirror of the planar unit-distance theorem neighborhood. Every mathematical object that participates in the chain from Q to U(n) is promoted to its OWN first-class table, and every intermediate quantity (distance squared, edge count, density exponent, witness-consistency check, bound exponent, anchor match) is a first-class calculated/lookup/aggregation field on the entity to which it belongs. Nothing is hidden in a property bag, an expression tree, or a generic relation row. The Pythagorean test: if a mathematician would name it, it has its own column.

Declarative business rules rendered from the rulebook — the single source of truth. Every statement below is the plain-language reading of a formula; nothing here is hand-authored prose.

Use the in the top-right corner to turn each part of the documentation on or off — Docs, the literal reading, the raw formula, the author's description, and the links to a rule's inputs and consumers. Your choices are remembered.

n choose 2 — the trivial upper bound on UnitDistancePairCount.

In Docs

A point set's max possible edges is computed as the point count times the point count minus 1 divided by 2.

In plain words

(point count times (point count minus 1)) divided by 2.

As a formula
= Point Count*(Point Count-1)/2

ƒ Density Exponent Estimate Calculated 8 hops from ground truth decimal DR-9

The exponent c such that UnitDistancePairCount ≈ PointCount^c. Lower bounds for U(n) are claims that this exponent is ≥ some target for arbitrarily large PointCount.

In Docs

A point set's density exponent estimate is computed as the logarithm of the unit distance pair count divided by the logarithm of the point count.

In plain words

Log(unit distance pair count) divided by log(point count).

As a formula
= LOG(Unit Distance Pair Count)/LOG(Point Count)

ΣUnit Distance Pair CountPoint Set Count of point pairs whose point set is point set ID and is unit distance is yes. ΣPoint CountPoint Set Count of point set members whose point set is point set ID.

ƒ Is Auditable Via Its Pathway Calculated 14 hops from ground truth boolean DR-97

Pathway-appropriate audit gate. Algebraic-tower proofs need IsAlgebraicallyAnchored; combinatorial-pigeonhole proofs need obligations satisfied + finite witness consistent; witness-only claims just need WitnessConsistent. Fixes the bias of the older AlgebraicChainClosed gate, which would mis-rule Erdős's pigeonhole proof as 'not closed' simply because it doesn't use class field towers.

In Docs

An asymptotic lower bound is considered auditable-via-its-pathway if all of the following:

    • all of these hold:
      • the algebraic tower proof flag is set
      • the algebraically anchored flag is set
    • all of these hold:
      • the combinatorial proof flag is set
      • the all obligations satisfied flag is set
      • the witness consistent flag is set
    • all of these hold:
      • the proof pathway is “witness-only”
      • the witness consistent flag is set
In plain words

Is algebraic tower proof and is algebraically anchored, is combinatorial proof, all obligations satisfied, and witness consistent, or proof pathway is "witness-only" and witness consistent.

As a formula
= OR(AND(Is Algebraic Tower Proof, Is Algebraically Anchored), AND(Is Combinatorial Proof, All Obligations Satisfied, Witness Consistent), AND(Proof Pathway="witness-only", Witness Consistent))

superlinear-unit-distance-theorem-(autonomous-ai-proof,-2026) Superlinear Unit-Distance Theorem (autonomous-AI proof, 2026) U(n) > n^{1.014} for arbitrarily large n. First open problem central to a subfield of mathematics solved autonomously by AI — OpenAI's internal reasoning model produced the proof (inexplicit superlinear exponent) on 2026-05-20; Sawin's companion paper made the exponent explicit at 1.014 the same day. The model was general-purpose: not domain-trained, not scaffolded for proof search, not targeted at the unit-distance problem. Disproves Erdős 1946's polynomial-improvement conjecture (the long-held belief that square-grid constructions were optimal). true true OpenAI (2026-05-20) autonomous announcement + Sawin (2026), arXiv:2605.20579 1.014 true 1.014 true false false false U(n) true false 1 false 2026-05-20 — 2026-05-27 — true true true false false

↗ Bound is Currently Valid Lookup 1 hop from ground truth boolean DR-191

Surfaces the bound's curator-set IsCurrentlyValid onto the junction. Distinguishes 'bitemporally valid by date' from 'curator-confirmed valid'.

In Docs

A lower bound validity at snapshot's bound is currently valid when the linked asymptotic lower bound is currently valid.

In plain words

The is currently valid of the linked asymptotic lower bound.

As a formula
= INDEX(Is Currently Valid, MATCH(Asymptotic Lower Bound, Asymptotic Lower Bound ID, 0))

ƒ Is Curator Confirmed At This Snapshot Calculated 2 hops from ground truth boolean DR-192

Stricter than IsValidAtThisSnapshot: TRUE iff the bound is BOTH within its valid-time interval at this snapshot AND has been curator-confirmed (IsCurrentlyValid=TRUE). Excludes pending/unevaluated rows from 'as-of' rollups.

In Docs

A lower bound validity at snapshot is considered a curator confirmed at this snapshot if all of the following:

    • the valid at this snapshot flag is set
    • the bound is currently valid is true
In plain words

Is valid at this snapshot and bound is currently valid equals yes.

As a formula
= AND(Is Valid At This Snapshot, Bound is Currently Valid=TRUE)
